text.en: Meena saw the periodic table on the lab wall. "Elements in the same column behave alike," said her teacher.

The Modern Periodic Law says that the physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers. The table has seven periods, which are horizontal rows, and eighteen groups, which are vertical columns, and elements in a group have similar properties because they have the same number of outer electrons.
Periodic trends are patterns across a period and down a group. Atomic radius decreases across a period and increases down a group. Ionisation enthalpy, the energy to remove an electron, generally rises across a period and falls down a group, and electronegativity follows a similar pattern.
Metals lie on the left and centre, non-metals on the right and metalloids between them. Understanding periodic trends helps us predict reactions and uses of elements.
